# Cornelia Bryant

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019), [v4 c6 P40](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0040)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000)</sub>
- **Titles:** Miss  <sub>[v4 c6 P37](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0037)</sub>; Mrs. Marshall Elliott  <sub>[v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Miss Cornelia  <sub>[v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000), [v4 c6 P37](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0037)</sub>

## Appearance

She has a fresh, round, pink-and-white face, jolly brown eyes, and a hard little knob of fair hair secured by a tight elastic band. She wears glasses while embroidering and is known to wear odd attire, such as a striped blue-and-white apron over a chocolate print wrapper covered in huge pink roses.

_Sources: [v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019), [v4 c8 P20](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0020), [v4 c8 P22](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0022)_

## Personality

Miss Cornelia is an outspoken, opinionated, and independent woman who holds a strong prejudice against men and Methodists. Despite her bitter tongue, sharp tongue, and sarcastic comments, she possesses a deeply kind heart and is always among the first to render tender aid whenever there is trouble or need. She carries herself with immense natural dignity regardless of her surroundings or clothing.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P37](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0037), [v4 c6 P38](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0038), [v4 c6 P40](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0040), [v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019), [v4 c8 P20](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0020)_

## History

Miss Cornelia lived in a vibrant green house in Four Winds and established herself as a notable local figure known for her fierce devotion to the Presbyterian church and her outspoken dislike of men and Methodists. When Anne Blythe moved to the area as a bride, Miss Cornelia paid her a visit, bringing along baby clothes she was sewing for a struggling neighbor's upcoming child. Over time, she frequently visited the Blythe house to share news, local gossip, and lively debates with Captain Jim Boyd and Dr. Gilbert Blythe. She assisted Leslie Moore with house cleaning prior to Dick Moore's operation and helped support Leslie through financial and practical preparations. Eventually, despite her long-standing reputation as a man-hater, Miss Cornelia surprised the community by marrying Marshall Elliott. Thirteen years after her marriage, she continued to visit Anne and Gilbert at Ingleside to share local news and stay involved in the Glen St. Mary community.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P35](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0035), [v4 c6 P37](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0037), [v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019), [v4 c8 P21](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0021), [v4 c8 P23](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0023), [v4 c18 P28](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0028), [v4 c18 P42](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0042), [v4 c31 P0](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0000), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000), [v5 c1 P1](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0001), [v5 c1 P8](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0008)_

## Quotes

> I’ve brought my work, Mrs. Blythe, dearie. I’m in a hurry to get this done, and there isn’t any time to lose.  <sub>[v4 c8 P21](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0021)</sub>

> This is for Mrs. Fred Proctor up at the Glen. She’s expecting her eighth baby any day now, and not a stitch has she ready for it. The other seven have wore out all she made for the first, and she’s never had time or strength or spirit to make any more. That woman is a martyr, Mrs. Blythe, believe ME.  <sub>[v4 c8 P23](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0023)</sub>

> I am positive that Billy Booth is possessed by him now.  <sub>[v4 c18 P42](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0042)</sub>

> I shall never have truck or trade with Methodists, and Mr. Meredith will find that he’d better steer clear of them, too.  <sub>[v5 c2 P43](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0043)</sub>
